fiscal_year_end: Approximately January 30 (fiscal year FY2026 ended approximately January 30, 2026)
key_finding: Dell FY2026 produced $113.5B revenue with the operating story dominated by ISG: $24.6B FY26 AI server revenue (+300%+ YoY), $64B+ of AI-optimised server orders closed during the year, $25B+ of AI server shipments, and a record $43B AI server backlog entering FY27. ISG Q4 revenue $18.82B (+66%) with server and networking +112%. CSG Q4 revenue $13.5B (+14%) — commercial $11.6B (+16%), consumer $1.9B (flat). The AI server cycle is the dominant operating leverage event of the year; CSG provides the cash-generative base.
structural_observations: AI server revenue growing 300%+ YoY while CSG grows 14% indicates Dell's operating gravity has fundamentally shifted toward ISG within twelve months.
Backlog of $43B entering FY27 against $25B FY26 AI server shipments implies forward-deliverable revenue is roughly double the year just completed.

ISG +66% versus CSG +14% creates margin-mix uplift if AI server gross margin holds — though Dell does not separately disclose AI server gross margin and concerns exist that hyperscaler-volume AI server economics compress at scale.
CSG commercial +16% reflects the AI PC refresh cycle beginning; the consumer line at flat YoY reflects the continued weakness in discretionary PC spending.
September 2025 CFO transition (McGill out, Kennedy interim) creates a leadership-continuity question heading into the FY27 ramp; permanent CFO search announced.
